case.name: Project Bluebird Workshop (Group 1)
case.description: Group 1 case focused on S1 (Argument Over Reward-Component Attribution)

tree.name: G1
tree.description: The agent’s behaviour during the supervised operational trial is explainable to the degree necessary for operational supervision by ATCOs, developmental oversight by the trial engineering team, and regulatory evaluation by aviation authorities.

children.name: P2
children.description: The actions recommended are as effective as possible given the rewards on average

children.name: E6
children.description: Explore a large set of combinations of weights and calculate pareto front

children.name: E5
children.description: Perform sensitivity analysis of reward components - series of behaviours you want to quantify and then what the connection to observed behaviour is

children.name: P3
children.description: The reward attributions align with how air traffic controllers would assign it - question: should it just be tuned such that the behaviour if sensible to them and this is just an issue for devs?
children.assumption: The Air Traffic controllers assessing this should be sufficiently experienced

children.name: E8
children.description: Process of expert validation; survey for given examples?

children.name: P4
children.description: We can understand the connection between individual action recommended and the reward weights (local rather than global level), particularly important for e.g. situations well outside the average like storms
children.assumption: NOTE: an ATC is going to pay attention to safety first and foremost (not as a proportion) and then look at other weights

children.name: P5
children.description: The scenarios generated for training are sufficient in scope to test the reward attribution

children.name: P5
children.description: The reward attributions always are safe and understandable for edge cases ("explainability envelope testing")

children.name: E7
children.description: Run a large number of trials and the coverage over which reward attribution is sensible

children.name: E9
children.description: The agent's reward attributions are robust to an adversarial scenario generator

children.name: P6
children.description: The reward structure shows why the agent took a particular action rather than a counterfactual - helpful for explainability to agents and for debugging with developers (possibly for review rather than in ops) - helping to optimise as HITL element in training

children.name: S2
children.description: Argument Over Cognitive Compatibility and Controller Workload

children.name: S3
children.description: Argument Over Runtime Monitoring and Operational Envelope

children.name: S4
children.description: Argument Over Reversion and Handover Protocol
